Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients may face challenges in participating in the FOOTSTEP self-management foot care programme due to various physical limitations. According to one of the completed prompts, just over half of the patients in this present cohort are physically able to undertake some aspects of self-managed foot care, including nail clipping and filing, callus filing, and daily hygiene and inspection. This suggests that many RA patients may need support or assistance with certain tasks related to their foot care.

In contrast, another prompt found that older patients who refuse to participate in a self-management intervention in the Netherlands are more likely to be physically able-bodied, suggesting that physical mobility restrictions and other factors may influence an individual's willingness to participate. This highlights the importance of considering these physical limitations when designing and implementing self-management interventions for RA patients.

The completed prompt also mentions that there is a relationship between rheumatoid arthritis and periodontal disease, which can be beneficial in identifying patients who are at high risk for developing other conditions. Furthermore, another completed prompt found that patients with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and folic acid need to continue taking FA supplements over the long term to prevent treatment discontinuation due to side effects.

In terms of ambulatory process of care predicting health-related quality of life outcomes, one completed prompt suggested a significant relationship between better ambulatory process of care and better health-related quality of life. This finding underscores the importance of improving the process of care for RA patients.

Finally, another prompt found that limb-salvage surgery may offer patients better quality of life and functional capacity than amputation, but does not necessarily improve their perception of quality of life. This highlights the need to consider multiple factors when evaluating alternative treatments for RA patients.

Overall, the completed prompts suggest that many rheumatoid arthritis patients face physical challenges in participating in self-management foot care programs, and older patients may be more likely to be physically able-bodied. However, there is also a relationship between rheumatoid arthritis and periodontal disease, and limb-salvage surgery offers some benefits for RA patients over amputation. Further research is needed to confirm these findings and develop effective interventions that address the physical and psychosocial needs of RA patients.
